clinician.trajectory_summary: A Japanese preterm infant (36+3 weeks gestation, 1860g birth weight) was referred on day 1 of life with symptomatic congenital CMV infection. Maternal history included CMV seroconversion (positive IgG and IgM) with fever at 4 weeks gestation, and prenatal findings of fetal growth restriction and abnormal biophysical examination. At birth, positive CMV-DNA was confirmed in both urine and whole blood. The infant presented with multisystem involvement including hepatosplenomegaly, microcephaly, and intravertebral calcification. Ophthalmoscopic examination at admission revealed distinctive ocular findings: posterior vessel dilation and demarcation line at the temporal peripheral zone in both eyes, and arteriovenous anastomosis in the right eye, notably without chorioretinitis. Oral valgancyclovir was initiated within the first 5 days of life. By day 11 of life (6 days of antiviral therapy), complete regression of vessel dilation and remarkable improvement of the arteriovenous anastomosis were documented. At 3 months of age, fluorescein angiography showed almost complete regression of the arteriovenous anastomosis, but chorioretinal atrophy had developed at the macula and around the optic disc, representing late sequelae of CMV infection despite antiviral therapy.
